definition: The Bowler Communications System is an open protocol developed by Neuron Robotics for simplified communications between components in cyber-physical systems.
details: The Bowler Communications System is an open protocol developed by Neuron Robotics for simplified communications between components in cyber-physical systems.

explainer.lead: The Bowler Communications System, or BCS, is an open protocol created by Neuron Robotics to help the parts of a cyber-physical system communicate. It provides a shared way for components to exchange information instead of requiring a separate communication approach for each connection.

tiers.eli5: It's a shared language that lets the different parts of a machine talk to each other simply.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it to connect components in cyber-physical systems, and a pitfall is depending on a niche open protocol's ecosystem.
tiers.paperLevel: An open protocol developed by Neuron Robotics for simplified communications between components in cyber-physical systems.

explainer.example: In a simple cyber-physical setup, a sensor component could send a reading to a controller component using BCS. Both components would rely on the same protocol rather than requiring a one-off communication method for that connection.
explainer.intuition: BCS acts like a common language for the components of a cyber-physical system. By sharing one protocol, components can communicate without every connection needing its own custom arrangement.
howItWorks: A cyber-physical system contains components that need to exchange information.
Those components use BCS as their shared communication protocol.
BCS provides a common approach to component-to-component communication.
This reduces the need for separate communication arrangements between individual components.
explainer.whyItMatters: Communication between components is a basic requirement of cyber-physical systems. BCS addresses that requirement with an open protocol intended to make those interactions simpler.
misconceptions: BCS is not a robot or hardware device; it is a communications protocol.
Calling it open does not mean every cyber-physical system uses it.
Its purpose is communication between components, not control of a particular physical device.

diagram.caption: BCS provides a shared protocol for communication between cyber-physical system components.
